newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves rates steady, posts profits.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves rates steady, posts profits.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates steady after its regular meeting, in line with market expectations.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, remains fixed at three percent for the next two weeks.
The central bank also announced its 1996 profit at 9.43 billion marks ($5.5 billion) and said 8.83 billion marks were being transfered to the Bonn government.
In 1995 the Bundesbank posted a 10.93 billion mark profit and transferred to 10.32 billion marks to the government.
The government had budgeted for a seven billion mark transfer and will use the rest to retire old debt.
Economists had not expected any change on interest rates at this point as they argued inflation was still under control, eliminating the need to tighten rates at this time.

Economists also said that the central bank's monetary policy was already quite expansive and that there was little else the central bank could do to stimulate economic growth. Consequently a rate cut was also not expected.
The central bank last cut its discount and Lombard rates in April 1996.
